data.long_meaning: The one who calls, invites, or calls out towards the right path or Allah. The name Ayoub carries the meaning “The one who calls, invites, or calls out” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Ayoub usually hope their child will grow to embody the one who calls, invites, or calls out and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ayoub holds deep cultural significance in the Arab world. Ayoub is a popular name among Arabic speaking populations, particularly in countries like Egypt, Syria, and Jordan. The name Ayoub is also mentioned in several works of Arabic literature and folklore, most notably in the classic tale of Prophet Job (Ayoub in Arabic) as recounted in the Qur’an.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ayoub holds immense spiritual significance for Muslims around the world. Prophet Job is considered to be a highly revered figure in Islamic tradition, known for his unwavering faith in Allah despite facing numerous trials and hardships. The name Ayoub is thus a reminder of the importance of staying steadfast in one's faith and seeking Allah's guidance and help in times of hardship and adversity. Additionally, the term "Ayoub" is also used to refer to someone who invites others to the path of righteousness and encourages them to turn towards Allah. This spiritual meaning encourages individuals to spread the message of Islam and serve as a reminder to those around them to stay on the path of Allah.

historical_references.reference: Ayoub is believed to be the same person as the biblical Job in the Old Testament. The story of Job is one of the most ancient and enduring in all of literature. It is a tale of suffering and endurance, and the rewards of faith and righteousness. Job, a man of great wealth and blessings, is tested by God and loses everything he possesses, including his health. He remains steadfast in his faith and is eventually rewarded with all his blessings restored and even more.
historical_references.context: The Old Testament, Book of Job

historical_references.reference: The Islamic name Ayoub is derived from the Arabic word 'Ayoub' which means 'Job'. This name is popular among Arabs, and is mentioned in the Quran (Ayub in Arabic). The story of Ayoub is a part of the Islamic prophetic tradition, and is similar to the biblical account of Job. Ayoub is described as a righteous man who was tested by God, and was rewarded with his losses being restored.
